name: Accordion
description: Accordion is a single-player patience game where all cards are laid into one row and compressed into piles by matching suit or rank. A card can move onto the pile immediately to its left or three positions to its left. The goal is to finish with one pile.
origin: Europe (19th century, likely England or France)

overview.description: Accordion is a single-player patience game where all cards are laid into one row and compressed into piles by matching suit or rank. A card can move onto the pile immediately to its left or three positions to its left. The goal is to finish with one pile.
overview.origin: Europe (19th century, likely England or France)

history.origins: Rules for The Idle Year published by William Brisbane Dick (1883) and Tarbart (1905). Wood & Goddard (1940) recorded it as Tower of Babel. The name Accordion appears in the 1950s (Culbertson, Goren). Parlett equates Accordion with Idle Year, Methuselah and Tower of Babel.
timeline: 1883: Dick publishes strict rules (packet must move if possible).
1905: Tarbart publishes lax rules (judgment on whether to play).
1940: Wood & Goddard record as Tower of Babel.
1950s: Accordion name appears; Culbertson and Goren allow further deal before deciding moves.
history.cultural: Known as The Idle Year because a well-shuffled pack may require about a year to accomplish. Odds of winning ~1 in 100.
history.evolution: Originally cards were laid one at a time with moves only when no deal possible; modern rules adopt deal-then-play or play-as-you-go for better win odds.

setup.players: One player. Accordion is a patience (solitaire) game played by a single player; there are no opponents or partners.
setup.dealing: Deal cards one by one from stock into a single row. After each deal, resolve any legal compression moves before dealing again if playing the incremental style.
setup.equipment: One shuffled deck and table space for a long row of piles.

rules.objective: Compress the entire deck into a single pile. The game is won when all 52 cards are in one pile; the layout is so named because compressing the row resembles closing accordion pleats.
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal one card at a time into a row of face-up piles. 2. A top card may move onto the pile immediately to its left or three piles to its left if the destination top card matches suit or rank. 3. After a move, close gaps so piles stay contiguous. 4. Continue moving whenever legal moves exist. 5. Hand ends when no legal moves remain.
keyRules: Moves are always to the left.
A move is legal only when suit or rank matches the destination top card.
The allowed jump distances are exactly 1-left and 3-left.

strategy.basic: Identify four cards of the same rank close together near the end of the layout; move these sweeper cards as a group toward the front without covering them until the end.
strategy.intermediate: Prefer 3-left moves when they do not block future sweeper sequences. Preserve connector piles that enable multiple 3-left paths.
strategy.advanced: Treat the row as a dependency graph. Odds of winning are around one in a hundred. Alfred Sheinwold suggests considering five piles or fewer a win.
tips: Deal-all and play-as-you-go require different planning horizons.
Track sweeper ranks (four of a kind) near the right side.

variations.name: Deal-All First
variations.description: Deal all cards to the row first, then start moving.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation description only; base engine already models deal-then-play flow.

variations.name: Play-As-You-Go
variations.description: Deal one card at a time; resolve moves before dealing next. Original style, exceedingly difficult.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation description only; timing of moves is left to strategy, not engine overrides.

variations.name: Queen and Her Lad
variations.description: Jones 1892. Q♥ as commencing card, J♥ at bottom of stock. Discard cards between two of same suit/rank.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation noted for rules; custom layout and discards are not encoded as engine overrides yet.

variations.name: Royal Marriage
variations.description: Reduce deck to King and Queen of same suit, placed at start and end of layout.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes starting layout only; engine deck and phases remain shared with base game.

variations.name: Nidgi Novgorod
variations.description: 1904 Standard Hoyle. Two equal-rank cards at top/bottom of pack; deal 4 in row; discard inner cards when outer match.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation documented historically; its distinct mechanics are not modeled as separate overrides yet.

scoring.description: Score by final number of piles; fewer is better.

synthesis.shortDescription: A hard patience game where cards collapse leftward by suit-or-rank matches until no moves remain.
